questions.prompt: In a random sample of $n = 500$ manufactured components, the probability that a component exceeds a critical quality threshold is $p = 0.084$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the expected number of components in the sample that exceed the quality threshold.

questions.prompt: The lengths $X\text{ mm}$ of metal rods follow the normal distribution $X \sim \text{N}(100, 15^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a batch of 400 rods, find the expected number of rods that have length less than $85\text{ mm}$.

questions.prompt: A continuous random variable $Y$ follows a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a random sample of 600 observations of $Y$, find the expected number of observations that lie within $0.5$ standard deviations of the mean.

questions.prompt: The measurements $W$ in an industrial test are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a set of 300 measurements, find the expected number of measurements that differ from the mean by more than $1.5$ standard deviations.

questions.prompt: The journey times $T$ minutes taken by commuters on a bus route follow $T \sim \text{N}(48, 6^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a sample of 750 recorded journeys, find the expected number of journeys that take more than 57 minutes.

questions.prompt: An electronic item has probability $0.20$ of being defective (worth \$0) and probability $0.80$ of being sound (worth \$15).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the expected total monetary value of 50 such items.

questions.prompt: The masses $W$ grams of bags of flour filled by a machine are normally distributed with mean 1000 g and standard deviation 20 g, so that $W \sim \text{N}(1000, 20^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen bag contains less than 970 g of flour.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In a daily production batch of 1500 bags, find the expected number of bags that contain less than 970 g of flour.

questions.prompt: The wing lengths $X\text{ cm}$ of adult birds in a nature reserve follow $X \sim \text{N}(16.0, 0.5^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen bird has a wing length between $15.5\text{ cm}$ and $16.4\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In a biological study, 180 birds of this species are captured and measured. Find the expected number of birds with wing lengths between $15.5\text{ cm}$ and $16.4\text{ cm}$, and state an assumption required for this calculation.

questions.prompt: A furniture workshop produces study desks whose heights $H\text{ cm}$ are normally distributed with mean $70.0\text{ cm}$ and standard deviation $1.5\text{ cm}$, so that $H \sim \text{N}(70.0, 1.5^2)$. A student finds a desk comfortable only if the desk height is at least $9.0\text{ cm}$ greater than their seated knee height of $58.5\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly selected desk is comfortable for the student.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A school purchases a shipment of 250 of these desks. Calculate the expected number of desks that will be comfortable, and hence calculate the expected number that will not be comfortable.

questions.prompt: An agricultural cooperative grades freshly harvested oranges by diameter $D\text{ cm}$, where $D \sim \text{N}(7.0, 0.8^2)$. Oranges with diameter greater than $7.8\text{ cm}$ are graded as Large and sold for \$0.50 each. All other oranges are graded as Regular and sold for \$0.30 each.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the probability that a randomly chosen orange is graded as Large is $0.1587$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the expected financial revenue from a crate containing 1000 randomly selected oranges.

questions.prompt:
A precision engineering company produces quartz resonators. The deviation $X\text{ kHz}$ from nominal resonant frequency follows $X \sim \text{N}(0, 2.0^2)$. Resonators are classified into three quality grades:
- Grade A (High Precision): $|X| \le 2.0\text{ kHz}$, sold for \$8.00 each.
- Grade B (Standard): $2.0 < |X| \le 4.0\text{ kHz}$, sold for \$4.00 each.
- Grade C (Off-spec): $|X| > 4.0\text{ kHz}$, sold for scrap at \$1.00 each.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly selected resonator is classified as Grade A, and find the probability that it is classified as Grade C.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a resonator is classified as Grade B, and calculate the expected total revenue from a batch of 500 resonators.

questions.prompt: The operating lifespan $T$ hours of industrial temperature sensors follows the normal distribution $T \sim \text{N}(1200, 100^2)$. A sensor is designated as Super-Durable if its lifespan exceeds 1350 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen sensor is Super-Durable.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A warehouse receives a shipment of 2000 sensors. Calculate the expected number of Super-Durable sensors in the shipment, and calculate the variance of the number of Super-Durable sensors.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A testing facility tests a random sample of 8 sensors. Find the probability that the sample contains at least one Super-Durable sensor, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Trout harvested at a fish farm have weights $W$ grams distributed normally with mean $800\text{ g}$ and standard deviation $80\text{ g}$, so that $W \sim \text{N}(800, 80^2)$. The fish are sorted into three commercial size tiers:
- Small: $W < 700\text{ g}$
- Medium: $700 \le W \le 900\text{ g}$
- Large: $W > 900\text{ g}$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that a randomly chosen trout is classified into each of the three tiers: Small, Medium, and Large.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Small trout sell for \$3.50 each, Medium trout sell for \$6.00 each, and Large trout sell for \$9.00 each. Calculate the expected total revenue from a harvest of 800 trout.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A restaurant purchases a random selection of 4 trout from the farm. Find the probability that exactly 3 of the 4 trout are classified as Medium, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
